item.title: Trump: Iran war will end immediately after midterm election
item.description:
President Donald Trump told the press that he believes that the war with Iran will end immediately after the midterm election.
He explained: "They can't hold out any longer. They're desperate to try and affect the election so that we could get a nice, weak group of people in there and leave them alone and let them have their nuclear weapon."

item.title: IAEA sends Iran nuclear case to UN Security Council after 20 years
item.description: IAEA Board refers Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years over Tehran’s failure to cooperate with a probe into undeclared uranium.

item.title: Poll: Smotrich and Feiglin win 8 seats, Winter fails to cross threshold
item.description: Channel 14 poll shows the right-wing bloc winning 64 seats, compared to 44 for the anti-Netanyahu bloc.

item.title: ‘Proud British Jew’ Miliband pushes back on Chief Rabbi’s sanctions warning
item.description: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband rejects Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis’ warning that sanctions on Judea and Samaria could fuel antisemitism in Britain.

item.title: Following Haaretz report: Netanyahu demands investigation of journalists
item.description: Likud demands an investigation into the newspaper and three of its writers over allegations that senior PA official Mohammed Dahlan was involved in the publication of a false report.

item.title: Katz: Israel struck Iran twice, ‘when Necessary, we’ll Strike a third time’
item.description: From Mount Hermon, Defense Minister Katz vows Israel will remain in the Syrian security zone and warns that Iran could face a third Israeli strike.

item.title: Blinken on report he rejected Hamas offer to return hostages after Oct. 7th
item.description:
Biden-era Secretary of State Antony Blinken denied a Haaretz report that Qatar conveyed a Hamas offer to return the hostage immediately after the October 7th massacre and that he rejected it.
"For the record, this is false. Complete fiction," Blinken stated.

item.title: UK politician Nigel Farage tells Min. Sa'ar he would work to reverse anti-Israel measures
item.description:
Israeli Foreign Minister Giden Sa'ar spoke on Wednesday with Reform UK leader Nigel Farage following the anti-Israel moves by the Labour Government.
Sa'ar thanked Farage for his and his party’s support for Israel. Farage shared that he was pleased to have addressed the Reform Friends of Israel event at the party conference in Birmingham last week.
The British politician also assured Sa'ar that, in government, Reform UK would reverse the damage done to the UK-Israel relationship by the Labour Government and its policies.

item.title: StandWithUs Co-Founder: 'Right-wing parties must unite to prevent wasted votes'
item.description: Dr. Shmuel Katz urges Israelis abroad to participate in the elections and calls on smaller right-wing parties to unite, warning that votes for parties that fail to cross the electoral threshold could ultimately weaken the right.

item.title: From New York City Hall to Israeli tech: Eric Adams joins TurboGen
item.description: Former NYC Mayor Eric Adams joins Israeli energy company TurboGen’s Advisory Board, helping drive US expansion and new opportunities for its power technology.

item.title: Iran’s new demands from US: $24 billion, Yemen, Lebanon and nukes
item.description: IRGC says war with the US could end if Washington meets Tehran’s demands on frozen assets, nuclear and missile programs, Yemen and Lebanon.

item.title: ‘Economic discrimination’: Jewish leaders blast sanctions on Israelis
item.description: Jewish leaders warn the measures targeting Israeli businesses in Judea and Samaria will isolate Israel, undermine cooperation and hinder peace efforts.

item.title: Tzvika Mor: “The British are worse than the Nukhba terrorists"
item.description: The father of captivity survivor Eitan Mor and Religious Zionism Knesset candidate sharply attacks British sanctions on Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria.

item.title: National Public Diplomacy Director: Israeli intel cooperation with UK will be reduced
item.description: Tzipi Hotovely, head of Israel’s National Public Diplomacy Directorate, told Channel 12 News that following the boycott targeting Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria, “our intelligence cooperation with Britain will be reduced."

item.title: ‘The fight of my life’: Police Spokesman recalls battle for truth after 10/7
item.description: Israel Police spokesman Dean Elsdunne speaks to Arutz Sheva about October 7, the battle for Israel’s truth abroad, and why Israelis must keep speaking out.

item.title: What Israel's response to Britain should have been
item.description: Why all the other signatories of Foreign Secretary Miliband’s antisemitic initiative weren’t also sanctioned by having their consulates in Jerusalem closed is totally beyond me.

item.title: PM at Hermon summit: We won't allow any terror army to establish itself on our border
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the Mount Hermon summit with the defense minister. “The main task is to defeat the terror regime in Iran. We are close to achieving that."

item.title: US Assessment: Iran plans to use Pickaxe Mountain as shelter for nuclear program
item.description: US officials assess that Iran plans to use the “Pickaxe Mountain" nuclear site as a shelter for its nuclear program, CNN reports.

item.title: To Britain: Peace requires recognizing Jewish rights, not destroying them
item.description: If Jews do not have the right to live, then ipso facto, Palestinian Arabs have the right to kill them, and it is not murder to do so. Does that bring us closer to peace? Opinion.

item.title: Israeli Ambassador to Hungary: 'Budapest doesn't want to see Jews living in ghettos.'
item.description: Ambassador Maya Kadosh tells Arutz Sheva that Hungary’s zero-tolerance policy toward antisemitism allows Israelis and Jews to feel safe in Budapest, while warning of antisemitic rhetoric from the far right.

item.title: No Shofar on Shabbat
item.description: The Sages decreed not to blow the shofar out of fear that a single Jew who does not know how to blow might carry his shofar on Shabbat in a public domain. For the sake of that single Jew, we suspend the mitzvah of shofar-blowing that year for all the people of Israel!

item.title: NY Governor pledges $70 million for synagogue security
item.description: New York State Governor Kathy Hochul announced that $70 million would be spent on providing security for synagogues ahead of the start of the Jewish High Holidays.

item.title: Critically wounded in Lebanon, soldier returns to IDF
item.description: Nearly two years after fighting for his life, Itamar Galinsky returns to reserve duty in the same unit where he was wounded. 'The nation of Israel lives!'
